title: Positivity of Serre's Intersection Multiplicity
main_claim: Serre's positivity conjecture in full generality, including ramified mixed characteristic: for nonzero finite modules M,N over a regular local ring with finite-length tensor product and dim M + dim N = dim R, chi(M,N) > 0. The proof has two Galois norm comparisons. (1) Rational K-theory with closed supports descends along finite covers whose geometric fibers are transitive (Thm ds:descent). This gives |G_D| a_D a_E chi(D,E) = sum_sigma c_sigma, where c_sigma is a normalized Euler characteristic against a perfectoid/perfection length algebra C_D. (2) The same descent, applied in an asymptotic "rank quotient" category with a connective coefficient algebra H, gives |G_E| c_sigma = sum_gamma b_{sigma,gamma}. Each b is bounded below by nu_sigma*eta_E > 0, using finite-length approximations M_n of C_D/xC_D, truncated minimal resolutions, and a degree-zero generator bound.

issues.location: Section 3 (descent.tex), Theorem ds:descent and Lemma ds:finite-surjection; used with exotic H in Thm as:norm
issues.description: The whole argument rests on one K-theoretic input: rational K-theory supported on V(J) (with p in J) is a cdh sheaf with finite-flat descent, hence has descent for finite surjections and orbit descent, even with an arbitrary connective associative coefficient algebra H. In the application H is the endomorphism dg-algebra of a Drinfeld quotient of prod_n M_{s_n}(A), which is huge and non-Noetherian. The individual steps hold up formally as far as I checked. E is truncating via Goodwillie (the HN terms cancel). The finite-flat retract argument holds, and so does the flattening-by-blowup induction. The section-translate abstract-blowup square also holds. For commutative H the statement agrees with known h-descent of rational KH. However, the paper applies Land-Tamme cdh descent with coefficients (their Appendix B) to this non-finite-type H and does not check that reference's hypotheses explicitly. I could not verify that independently. It is a load-bearing citation, not a demonstrated error.
issues.evidence: descent.tex: 'Truncating localizing invariants satisfy cdh descent, also after tensoring with a fixed connective associative algebra over the base [LT, Theorem A.2 and Appendix B, especially Theorem B.3]'; asymptotic.tex Lemma as:connective builds H = End_{P_A}(q_A E_A) from B_A = prod_n M_{s_n}(A).

issues.description: Sanity check, not an error. In characteristic p the length on C = T_perf is G-invariant. So Lemma ds:ordinary-norm implies that chi_T = chi_infinity (the Dutta multiplicity) for every perfect complex with finite-length homology over any normal complete local domain T that is Galois over a regular local base. I tested this on the Dutta-Hochster-McLaughlin ring k[[x,y,z,w]]/(xy-zw), with Z/2 swapping z and w over k[[x,y,z+w]]. The norm sum chi(M,R/(x,z)) + chi(M,R/(x,w)) = chi(M,R/x) = 0 behaves as the theorem predicts. So no contradiction was found, but the descent statement is strong, and a counterexample of this kind (non-Roberts T, Galois over a regular ring) would refute it.
issues.evidence: Equation ds:ordinary-norm-identity plus G-invariance of the perfection length; the DHM computation via 0 -> R/(x,w) --z--> R/(x) -> R/(x,z) -> 0.
